change.author: Joe Au-Yeung

findings.title: Google refresh now saves the zod SafeParse wrapper as the credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `safeParse`, which is `{ success, data }`. The old code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returns just the data. Line 100 now writes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` into `credential.key`. On the next request, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75 throws because `access_token`/`refresh_token` are no longer at the top level, so every Google Calendar credential breaks after its first token refresh. This happens for all installs, not only ones with credential sharing on. Fix: use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` as the key (salesforce, zoom and office365 already read `.data`).

findings.title: Sync mode returns a fetch Response, which has no `.data`
findings.body: When sharing is on, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` Response (`_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15`). `res?.data` is then undefined, so `token.access_token` at line 95 throws a TypeError. The catch at line 108 swallows it because the message is not `invalid_grant`, so the token is never refreshed and nothing reports why. The response body has to be read with `await res.json()` in the sync branch.

findings.title: HubSpot sync mode stores a fetch Response as the credential
findings.body: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` Response, not the `HubspotToken` that `createToken` returns. `expiresIn` is undefined, so `expiryDate` becomes NaN. Line 198 then writes the Response object (which serializes to `{}`) as `credential.key`, and line 202 sets an undefined access token. Without an error the stored credential is wiped, and the catch only logs. The sync response needs `json()` plus a mapping to the HubSpot token shape.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential id as the user id
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id where the helper expects `userId` (`refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3,11`). The sync endpoint then receives `calcomUserId=<credential id>` and returns tokens for the wrong user, or none. Also, in sync mode the result is a fetch Response, so `tokenInfo.data.error` at line 96 throws. The zohocrm `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` (zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217) has the same `.data` problem.

findings.title: `prisma` is not imported; in production it resolves to an undefined global
findings.body: This file never imports `@calcom/prisma`. `prisma` only type-checks because of the `declare global { var prisma }` in packages/prisma/index.ts:6-8. That global is only assigned when `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (packages/prisma/index.ts:58-60), so in production `prisma.credential.update` throws, `getClient` rejects, and every Salesforce CRM operation fails. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes on every instantiation, then ignores the new token
findings.body: `getClient` runs from the constructor and now refreshes the token unconditionally each time a `SalesforceCalendarService` is created, with no expiry check. That adds a token request per booking operation and risks Salesforce rate limits. The fresh token is also never used: line 106 still passes the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` to `jsforce.Connection`. This path also skips `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is not honoured here. Line 86's `statusText !== "OK"` check fails on HTTP/2 responses, where `statusText` is empty; use `response.ok`.

findings.title: Computed keys in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` don't express "any key"
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`, so the second entry overwrites the first. The resulting schema is `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. `z.object` strips unknown keys, so in sync mode `expires_in`/`expiry_date` and every other field are dropped. Zoom and Office365 then store tokens with no expiry: office365's `isExpired(expires_in)` check at line 279 and zoom's expiry handling don't get the field they need, which causes repeated refreshes or a broken key. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` (or `.catchall(z.unknown())`).

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token can overwrite the real one
findings.body: When the response has no `refresh_token`, the helper writes the literal string "refresh_token". Office365 spreads the parsed data over the stored credentials (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264), so the user's real refresh token is replaced with "refresh_token" in the DB. If sync is later turned off, refreshes fail. Consider leaving the field unset so callers keep the stored value.

findings.title: Webhook secret check: plain `!==`, any HTTP method, unhandled throws
findings.body: This endpoint can write OAuth credentials for any user, and it is guarded only by a `!==` string comparison, which is not constant-time. Consider `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. The handler also accepts any method rather than only POST. Malformed bodies (`parse` at line 31), a wrong encryption key (`symmetricDecrypt` at line 58) and non-JSON plaintext (`JSON.parse`) all throw and return a generic 500 instead of a 400.

contracts.equivalent_path: Old code: myGoogleAuth.refreshToken -> res.data -> googleCredentialSchema.parse -> prisma update
contracts.before_after: Before, the parsed data was stored; now the SafeParse wrapper {success,data} is stored
contracts.visible_effect: Google calendar stops working after the first refresh because credential.key no longer parses
contracts.failure_mode: In sync mode, Response.data is undefined -> TypeError is swallowed by the catch -> stale token, nothing logged

contracts.action: Salesforce getClient refreshes the token and writes it through the global prisma
contracts.equivalent_path: zoom VideoApiAdapter refresh, which imports prisma and checks expiry first
contracts.before_after: No expiry check; the Connection still uses the old access token
contracts.failure_mode: globalThis.prisma is undefined in production -> TypeError -> conn promise rejects

contracts.action: Sync-mode refresh returns a fetch Response to callers that expect SDK or axios results
contracts.equivalent_path: Lark/Office365/Webex/Zoom pass a Response to handleErrorsJson; HubSpot/Zoho/Google expect parsed objects
contracts.before_after: HubSpot, Zoho CRM, Zoho Bigin and Google break; the fetch-based adapters work
contracts.visible_effect: Integrations silently stop refreshing, and HubSpot's key is overwritten
contracts.failure_mode: No timeout or error handling on the sync endpoint fetch

summary: The credential-sync feature introduces regressions that also hit installs where sharing is off. Google refresh now stores the zod SafeParse wrapper as the credential key, and Salesforce uses an unimported `prisma` that is undefined in production while also refreshing on every instantiation. With sync on, the fetch Response breaks HubSpot, Zoho and Google, Bigin sends the credential id as the user id, and the "minimum" schema's computed keys strip the expiry fields.
